title: A loop stalled on the spend limit reaches the person who can clear it
goal: The build loop sat still for sixty two hours because the monthly spend limit was reached, and the only thing that can clear it is a person raising the limit. The loop handled it correctly in every other way, but it says so only in the terminal window it runs in and in the dashboard hero, so unless somebody happens to be looking at one of those, the stall is silent for days. Nothing shipped for two and a half days and two daily digests were never written. Make the loop tell the person who can act, once, so a stall costs hours instead of days. This serves the ui-building focus by buying back the days the focus loses when nobody knows the loop has stopped: the last stall cost sixty two hours of focus work.
notes:
Found by the 2026-09-12 triage pass, from queue/history.jsonl.

The outage: the last task finished 2026-09-09T17:37Z and the next finished 2026-09-12T08:26Z, sixty two hours later. Across it the loop recorded 128 consecutive runner_failed events with reason "spend", one every thirty minutes, plus 38 digest_deferred events. The digests for 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-11 were never written.

What the loop already does right, and must not be changed: it reads the refusal out of the runner's own words, marks it an environment failure, counts nothing against the task, never parks anything, backs off to thirty minutes, banners the Ghoztty window (go-loop.sh:248-253), retitles it "photonz: go-loop (spend limit)", and resumes on its own the moment the limit clears. It did all of that. The recovery was clean: eleven tasks finished in the three and a half hours after it resumed.

The gap is only reach. There is no osascript, no notification, nothing that leaves the terminal window (grep for osascript or notify in go-loop.sh returns nothing).

This serves the unmanned-loop epic, which is staged next, and it is filed at p2 rather than p3 because it is the single largest loss of focus work this cycle: two and a half days of ui-building progress that the loop could not make and could not ask for.

queue/bin/failure-drill.sh already runs the real loop against fake runners, so it is the place to prove this.

Same cause, worth knowing when you build this: six decision cards are sitting unanswered on the dashboard and five of them have been waiting since 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09, right through the stall. They freeze five p2 tasks. The loop is not short of ways to say something; it is short of a way to reach somebody who is not looking at the dashboard. If this lands well, a question that has waited a day is the obvious next thing to carry, but that is a separate task and not this one.

DEP ADDED 2026-09-13 by the manager pass: a-runner-that-talks-about-the-spend-limit-is-not must land first. The loop currently classifies a runner that merely MENTIONS the spend limit as one that hit it (reproduced on that task), so shipping the notification before the fix would send the person to raise a limit that is fine.
acceptance: When the loop hits a refusal only a person can clear, the spend limit or a sign-in, it raises a macOS notification naming what is wrong and what to do
It notifies once per stall, not once per retry, so a long stall is one notification and not a hundred and thirty
It notifies again if the stall is still going a day later, so a stall that outlives the first notice is not forgotten
Clearing the limit and letting the loop resume sends nothing, and the notification is proven by the failure drill rather than by hand
The behaviour is written into queue/README.md beside the rest of the failure handling

log.note: a-runner-that-talks-about-the-spend-limit-is-not landed first, as its notes asked: a refusal is now only believed from the CLI's own channel, so this notification cannot fire on a healthy loop that merely filed a task about the limit. Read status.lastError.reason, which is now trustworthy.

Built it. queue-lib.mjs advanceStall() decides WHEN somebody is disturbed (status.json gains a stall record: reason, since, notifiedAt, notices, attempts); recordRunnerExit returns notify + stallHours; queue.mjs runner-exit prints NOTIFY/STALLHOURS; go-loop.sh notify_person() decides WHAT IT SAYS and raises it with osascript, called from backoff_wait. Adversarial review before building: a notification per retry would have been 128 of them and worse than none, so the rule is once at the start plus once per day; a modal dialog would steal focus, and email needs config nobody has; a recovery ping teaches people to ignore the next one, so recovery is silent.

Proven two ways. failure-drill.sh scenario 6 runs the REAL loop three times over one sandbox queue: four refusals in a row raise exactly one notification naming the limit and the URL, the same stall aged 25h on status.json raises a second saying 'Still stopped 25h later', raising the limit sends nothing and clears the stall record, and the held-up task and digest then land. Plus advanceStall replayed against the actual 2026-09-09 stall (half-hourly for 62 hours) = 3 notices, 125 attempts. Every drill scenario now runs with a stand-in osascript on PATH so a drill can never reach the real Notification Center. All six scenarios pass; the other six queue drills and Scripts/test.sh (7303 tests) pass too.

Verified the notification really lands, not just that osascript exits 0: /usr/bin/log show over usernoted records 'Presenting <NotificationRecord app:com.apple.ScriptEditor2> as banner ([badge, sound, alert])' and 'Delivering ... to [.alert .lockScreen .notificationCenter]'. Lock-screen delivery matters here: a stall while the Mac is locked still reaches them. Screen capture is denied to this terminal so there is no picture of it; said so in the audit rough.

Fixed on the way, in scope because I needed the drill green: failure-drill.sh computed today's date with toISOString (UTC) while the loop names digests after date +%F (local), so scenarios 2, 3 and 5 failed every evening between 5pm Pacific and midnight on source that was fine. Reproduced on unmodified main with git stash before touching it. The loop's own regression check was broken seven hours a day.

left rough, not filed because I could not reproduce it and the bar says an unreproduced problem does not jump the queue: if the spend limit lands mid-task with exactly ONE ready task, that task is parked after three tries and the loop then idles quietly, so the first notification fires but the day-later one never does (nothing is retrying to notice). With two or more tasks the streak blames the environment, nothing is parked, and the daily notice works. Also in the audit rough.

The loop now raises a macOS notification when it stalls on a refusal only a person can clear: once at the start, once more per day it lasts, nothing on recovery. advanceStall in queue-lib.mjs decides when (stall record on status.json), notify_person in go-loop.sh decides what it says, called from backoff_wait. Proven by failure-drill.sh scenario 6 (three real loop runs: four refusals = one notification, the same stall a day later = a second saying how long, limit raised = silence and a cleared record) plus advanceStall replayed against the real 62-hour stall = 3 notices not 128. Delivery confirmed in the system log as a banner with sound to the alert, lock screen and Notification Center. Documented in queue/README.md. Also fixed the drill's UTC-vs-local date bug that failed three scenarios every evening. All 6 drill scenarios, the other 6 queue drills and Scripts/test.sh (7303 tests) pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-15-loop-stall-notification.json. Commit 31903b4c, pushed.
